Degree Engineering (Electrical Engineering Track) New Online Option Noncredit New for Spring 2026 Program Description Pending state approval. Please check with the CTE Division Office for status. This program is designed to provide students with a comprehensive academic foundation in electrical engineering principles, preparing them for seamless transfer to four-year institutions. This program ensures that students acquire the necessary theoretical knowledge and practical skills to successfully continue their education in a bachelor's degree program in electrical engineering or related fields. In addition to preparing students for academic advancement, the program also supports local career pathways by equipping them with fundamental technical skills essential for various engineering-related professions. Students will gain hands-on experience and problem-solving abilities that align with industry needs, enabling them to pursue opportunities in sectors such as electronics, power systems, telecommunications and automation. With a flexible curriculum, the program caters to students with diverse career goals. Whether they choose to continue their education at a university or seek entry-level engineering roles, graduates of this program will be well-prepared to meet the demands of the evolving engineering industry. Program Learning Outcomes Upon completion, students will be able to Apply foundational electrical engineering principles, analytical reasoning and hands-on techniques to identify and solve basic engineering problems Apply knowledge of mathematics, physics, chemistry and engineering to formulate, model and analyze problems involving electrical and electronic systems Demonstrate programming, algorithmic thinking and computational problem-solving in the context of engineering applications Communicate and collaborate effectively in team-based engineering projects by presenting technical work through written reports, oral presentations and design documentation Demonstrate the ability to transfer engineering knowledge and skills to real-world or simulated industry scenarios, preparing for upper-division coursework and entry-level roles in electrical engineering fields De Anza College Requirements Noncredit Certificate Requirements Each course listed as a program requirement must be completed with a C grade, passing grade or satisfactory progress Each course must be completed at De Anza College Skills Certificate Requirements Skills Certificates are awarded by departments and are not notated on official college transcripts. Contact the department directly for assistance in applying for a skills certificate. Completion of all major courses with a C grade or higher Each course must be completed at De Anza College Certificate of Achievement Requirements Certificates of Achievement are awarded by the college and notated on official transcripts. Each course listed as a program requirement must be completed with a letter grade of C or higher. Pass/No Pass grades are not accepted for these courses. No more than six quarter units may be transferred from other academic institutions Certificate of Achievement-Advanced Requirements Certificates of Achievement-Advanced are awarded by the college and notated on official transcripts. Each course listed as a program requirement must be completed with a letter grade of C or higher. Pass/No Pass grades are not accepted for these courses. Students must demonstrate proficiency in English and Mathematics by qualifying for ENGL C1000, ENGL C1000H or ESL 5, and by qualifying for MATH 114 or a transfer-level Math course No more than 18 quarter units may be transferred from other academic institutions Cal-GETC Certificate of Achievement-Advanced Requirements See Cal-GETC pattern found at deanza.edu/articulation/ge-requirements .
